headline: Gulf Tension Lifts Crude as Thursday Opens Behind a Strong Chip-Led Session
body_html:
Traders face a Thursday open shadowed by the Gulf. Crude climbed overnight as Middle East tension escalated. Iran's IRGC Navy said seven vessels had been hit and warned Washington of a wider response, and an attack on an airport in the Saudi oil city of Dammam left two dead.

Wednesday's session leaves a constructive backdrop. Of the 544 stocks we track, 320 rose and 219 fell. Semiconductors led the sector table, up 2.25%, ahead of energy at 1.16%, industrials at 1.05% and software at 0.89%. Consumer shares slipped 1.43% and homebuilders gave back 1.12%.

At the open, watch whether oil-services names extend gains while crude stays firm. Weatherford rose 7.75% on Wednesday. Also watch whether security software holds its bounce, after Zscaler gained 7.84% and Okta 7.54%. Consumer laggards such as Winmark and Celsius, which fell 7.97% and 5.51%, need to stabilize. The dollar's recent dip has paused with the Fed in focus, so rate-sensitive groups may be choppy. Early prices are thin and unreliable, so the first hour's direction matters more than the first print.

briefs.headline: Iranian naval force warns of wider response
briefs.body: The IRGC Navy said seven vessels had been struck and cautioned the United States that it could respond more broadly. The warning raises the risk premium on shipping lanes and energy. Traders will watch whether the rhetoric turns into action once Thursday's session begins.

briefs.headline: Airport attack in Dammam jolts oil hub
briefs.body: Two people were killed and eight injured in an attack on an airport in Dammam, a Saudi oil city. The strike adds to supply-security worries already supporting crude. Energy shares, which rose 1.16% on Wednesday, are in focus at the open.

briefs.headline: Bank of Korea pauses after two hikes
briefs.body: South Korea's central bank held rates steady, as markets had expected, following back-to-back increases. The pause suggests policymakers want to gauge how earlier tightening is working while energy-driven price pressures stay elevated. Regional currencies and bond markets are the places to watch.

briefs.headline: Dollar's slide pauses ahead of Fed
briefs.body: The recent dip in the dollar has taken a breather as attention turns to the Federal Reserve. A steadier currency could ease some pressure on commodity prices and overseas earnings. Any shift in rate expectations could quickly reset the tone for growth stocks.

briefs.headline: India's Mideast crude buying is back to pre-war pace
briefs.body: India's oil imports from the Middle East returned to pre-war levels in September. Commentators caution that the rebound should not be read as a return to normal, given the ongoing tension. High fuel costs continue to reach everyday spending, from food to mortgages.

briefs.headline: AI race and French debt anchor the morning agenda
briefs.body: Morning previews point to two themes: strain in French government debt and a continuing AI funding push. DeepSeek is reportedly finishing a large fundraising round. Semiconductors led Wednesday's gains at 2.25%, so AI-linked sentiment is a key read at the open.
